blocks.text: OSTREVIA (lumiravostat) is indicated for the treatment of adults with moderate to severe chronic hand eczema that has not responded adequately to potent topical corticosteroids, or when these are not advisable.
Pediatrics (< 18 years of age): No data are available to Health Canada; therefore, Health Canada has not authorized an indication for pediatric use.
Geriatrics (≥ 65 years of age): Clinical studies included too few patients aged 65 and over to determine whether they respond differently. Use with caution.

items: Patients who are hypersensitive to lumiravostat or to any ingredient in the formulation, including any non-medicinal ingredient. For a complete listing, see 6 DOSAGE FORMS, STRENGTHS, COMPOSITION, AND PACKAGING.
Patients with active tuberculosis or an active serious infection.

blocks.text:
Serious Warnings and Precautions
• Serious infections leading to hospitalization or death, including tuberculosis, have occurred (see 7 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS, Immune).
• Malignancies, including lymphoma, have occurred (see 7 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS, Carcinogenesis and Genotoxicity).
• Thrombosis, including pulmonary embolism, has occurred (see 7 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS, Hematologic).
Screen for latent tuberculosis and check blood counts and liver enzymes before starting treatment (see 7 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS).
The recommended dose is 10 mg once daily, with or without food. The dose may be increased to 25 mg once daily if the response is inadequate after 12 weeks.
Moderate hepatic impairment: 10 mg once daily. Severe hepatic impairment: not recommended.
With strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (for example ketoconazole or clarithromycin): 10 mg once daily.
Renal impairment: no dose adjustment.
Swallow tablets whole with water, with or without food.
If a dose is missed, take it as soon as possible unless the next dose is due within 12 hours. Do not take two doses at once.
There is no specific antidote. Monitor the patient for signs of adverse reactions and give supportive treatment. Lumiravostat is not removed by haemodialysis to a meaningful extent.
For management of a suspected drug overdose, contact your regional poison control centre.

Carcinogenesis and Genotoxicity: Malignancy, including lymphoma and non-melanoma skin cancer, has been reported. Consider the risks and benefits before starting treatment in patients with a known malignancy.
Hematologic: Venous thromboembolism, including deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, has been reported. Use with caution in patients with risk factors and stop treatment if it occurs.
Hepatic/Biliary/Pancreatic: Elevations of liver enzymes have occurred. Interrupt treatment if drug-induced liver injury is suspected.

Immune: Serious infections, including tuberculosis, pneumonia, cellulitis and herpes zoster, have been reported, some leading to hospitalization or death. Screen patients for latent tuberculosis before starting treatment and treat it first. Interrupt treatment if a serious infection develops.
Monitoring and Laboratory Tests: Monitor lymphocyte and neutrophil counts, haemoglobin and liver enzymes at baseline, at 4 weeks and every 3 months.

Lumiravostat caused embryo-fetal toxicity in rats and rabbits. It is contraindicated in pregnancy. Women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for 4 weeks after the last dose.
It is not known whether lumiravostat passes into human milk. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 4 days after the last dose.
Safety and efficacy have not been established.
Infections were more frequent in patients aged 65 and over.
The most common adverse reactions (≥ 10%) were nasopharyngitis. Serious infections, malignancy and thrombosis are described in 7 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS.

Clinical trials are conducted under very specific conditions. The adverse reaction rates observed in the clinical trials, therefore, may not reflect the rates observed in practice and should not be compared to the rates in the clinical trials of another drug.

items: 1. Why am I using OSTREVIA? It contains lumiravostat and is used to treat long-lasting hand eczema in adults.
2. What should I know before I use OSTREVIA? Do not use it if you are allergic to it, have an active serious infection or tuberculosis, or are pregnant.
3. What if I am taking other medicines? Some medicines may interfere with OSTREVIA.
4. How do I use OSTREVIA? Take one tablet once a day.
5. What should I know while using OSTREVIA? Tell your doctor straight away if you have signs of infection.
6. Are there any side effects? Common side effects include cold symptoms, headache and acne. Serious side effects include infections and blood clots.

blocks.text: OSTREVIA contains the active ingredient lumiravostat. It calms the immune activity that causes long-lasting hand eczema when creams have not worked well enough.

sections.title: What should I know before I use OSTREVIA?

blocks.text: Do not use OSTREVIA if you are allergic to lumiravostat or any of the ingredients listed at the end of this leaflet, if you have tuberculosis or another serious infection, or if you are pregnant.
Check with your doctor if you have had tuberculosis, cancer or blood clots, or have liver problems.

sections.title: What if I am taking other medicines?

blocks.text: Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are taking any other medicines, including any medicines, vitamins or supplements that you buy without a prescription. Some antifungals, antibiotics and St John’s wort may interfere with OSTREVIA.
Take one tablet once a day, with or without food. Swallow it whole with water. If you forget a dose, take it as soon as you remember, unless the next dose is due within 12 hours.

sections.title: What should I know while using OSTREVIA?

rows: Tell your doctor straight away if you have a fever, cough or a painful swollen leg.
Do not stop taking it or change the dose without checking with your doctor.
Store below 30°C in the original pack.

blocks.text: All medicines can have side effects. If you do experience any side effects, most of them are minor and temporary.

rows: Speak to your doctor if you have any of these less serious side effects and they worry you.
Fever, cough, painful blistering rash; pain or swelling in a leg, chest pain or sudden breathlessness
Call your doctor straight away, or go straight to the Emergency Department at your nearest hospital if you notice any of these serious side effects.

blocks.text: Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you notice anything else that may be making you feel unwell. Other side effects not listed here may occur in some people.

Reporting side effects: After you have received medical advice for any side effects you experience, you can report side effects to the Therapeutic Goods Administration online at www.tga.gov.au/reporting-problems.
This medicine is only available with a doctor’s prescription.

What OSTREVIA contains: lumiravostat 10 mg or 25 mg; inactive ingredients microcrystalline cellulose, mannitol, croscarmellose sodium, magnesium stearate; film coat: hypromellose, titanium dioxide, macrogol (25 mg tablets also iron oxide yellow). Do not take this medicine if you are allergic to any of these ingredients.

notice.title: Interstitial lung disease: new warning in every market
notice.text: A cumulative review found a causal association between lumiravostat and interstitial lung disease (ILD), including fatal cases. The CCDS now warns that patients should be told to report new or worsening cough, breathlessness or fever, and that treatment should be interrupted while ILD is investigated and stopped if it is confirmed. ILD is added to the post-marketing adverse reactions. Implement the wording in Canada, Switzerland, Japan and Australia and submit within 60 days.
